about: Reviewed identity decisions for src/data/sites.json. Applied by dedupe_sites.py apply; see hb_pipeline/site_merge.py for what each action does.

decisions.reason: The UNESCO property Samarra Archaeological City is the Abbasid capital's ruin-field itself, so the two cards described one site.
The mosque and shrine stand on the Nebi Yunus mound (Tell al-Tawba); the mound keeps its own card for the Assyrian palace beneath.
The stele was set up at Topzawa near Sidakan, the settlement site; its present custody (in place or in Erbil) is disputed.
A church in the modern town and the ancient mounds; they share only the town's name Karemlash.
Two shrines of Pir Mehmed Reshan, near Bardarash and on Mount Sinjar, about 150 km apart.
Churches of the same saint in two towns.
Separate entries in the Erbil archaeological site list.
Numbered sites of the same survey.
Survey sites TJ 11 and TJ 12 of the Kokushikan Tanjarow survey.
Different islands of the Haditha reservoir survey.
Different excavated Hamrin tells; only their proposed ancient names (Awal, Awalki) look alike.
Separate numbered entries on Yaseen's Hamrin map.
Sites 61 and 68 on Yaseen's Hamrin map.
Sites 45 and 56 on Yaseen's Hamrin map.
Different Haditha Dam survey records at different places (Sur Jur‘eh, Anah, Haditha, New Ma‘atheed); they share only the survey’s short description.
Two different buildings named in Kifri’s heritage list; only the short description is shared.
Different Hamrin tells worked by the Italian CRAST mission (Ubaid, Halaf and unstated periods).
Two Erbil Plain tells at different positions (about 30 km apart); the descriptions follow one template.
Different mosques in Rawa and Baghdad; the names share only "al-… Mosque".
Different mosques in Rawa and Kirkuk Citadel.
Different mosques in Baghdad and Mosul.
A Baghdad mosque and the Samarra shrine of the Imams.
The mosque stands on al-Maidan square; the square card covers the whole quarter.
The mosque stands on al-Rashid Street; the street card covers the whole avenue.
Three neighbouring churches of the old Christian quarter (Aqd al-Nasara); the Syriac Catholic church was built next to Om al-Ahzan.
Two churches 40 m apart in the old quarter of Alqosh.
A Syriac Catholic and a Syriac Orthodox church 60 m apart in Bashiqa.
Different tells on the Hamrin map; the names differ in their distinctive word.
Different villages about 28 km apart (Dehi in the Sapna valley, Dooreh in Barwari Bala); each has a church named after Mar Qayouma.
Different survey sites: Aliawa on the Erbil plain and Ali Awa on the Ranya–Pshdar plains; Ali Awa is a common village name.
A tell south of Erbil and a castle of Mosul’s city wall.
The citadel (قلعة) and the Ottoman barracks (قشلة) in the city centre; the Arabic names differ by two letters.
